title: Feedback stitch notebook and probe leds — June 2026
content:
Purpose:
Capture recent customer threads (May 28–June 11), synthesize recurring asks, and propose low-effort probes that CS + Eng can run in the next 2 sprints. This is intentionally a working notebook — raw notes, hypotheses, quick fixes, and risks.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Two dominant themes across 18 customers: 1) unpredictable tail latency for short-chat workloads after model warmups / cold starts; 2) customers asking for clearer model fallbacks and routing knobs in Hosted + Dedicated.
- Frequent secondary ask: clearer guidance and defaults for KV-cache usage with conversation-style workloads (prefix caching behaviour and cache invalidation semantics).
- Immediate low-effort probes: (A) targeted cold-start latency measurement job we can run on Dedicated pools (eng spike, 1 week); (B) a short doc + dashboard tile that surfaces routing/fallback rules per tenant (CS+Product, 2 days).

Raw signal highlights (representative snippets):
- "We see 300–500ms spikes even on 1-token responses after idle periods — not sure if this is model or infra" — enterprise fintech customer, thread Jun 2.
- "When KV cache seems stale, our app replays full context and costs double; need deterministic TTL or manual invalidation API" — healthcare startup, Jun 6.
- "Can we pin a cheaper quantized variant for background jobs and a full model for low-latency paths? Or at least policy guidance?" — marketplace SaaS, May 29.
- "During a canary swap the hosted route fell back to a much slower model and user-facing latency went up; no automatic alerting or suggested rollback." — in-product report, Jun 8.

Pattern synthesis and what it might mean: 
1) Cold-start / warmup tail is visible for short outputs: many customers operating chat snippets report spikes that look like per-request kernel selection or model memory load overhead. Hypothesis: runtime kernel selection + quantized variant loading on shared nodes causes short-lived spikes.
2) KV cache primitives are under-documented and default behavior surprises customers: ambiguity around when prefix/KV cache is used, how keys are derived, and what happens after model rollouts.
3) Routing/backoff policies exist but are opaque: customers want simple toggles (prefer-latency, prefer-cost, prefer-stability) exposed at route-level in Console + API, with previewed SLA tradeoffs.

Proposed quick probes (ranked by effort and expected signal):
- Probe 1 (effort: Xsprint): Dedicated cold-start profiler. Run an automated job that simulates 10k short-chat requests across 3 Dedicated pools (pinned models, mixed quantization) and capture per-step timings: kernel selection, model load, KV lookup, first-token latency. Deliverable: timeline trace + list of top 3 contributors to tail spikes. Owner: Evan Li (eng-serving-runtime). Linked: GITHUB: redwood-inference/serving-runtime#4123.

- Probe 2 (effort: 2d): KV-cache behavior note + example snippets. Create a short KB page describing explicit key derivation, how conversation prefixes map to cache entries, and a small JS/py SDK example that shows how to force invalidation. Deliverable: KB + copy for console tooltip. Owner: Priya Rao (CS).

- Probe 3 (effort: 1 sprint): Route-level policy UI mock + API schema. Product + Console to draft three policy presets (latency-first, cost-first, stable-fallback) and a telemetry preview panel showing estimated token-cost and median latency. Deliverable: mock + small prototype. Owner: Miguel Santos (product/console).

- Probe 4 (effort: 1 day): Canary rollback checklist + alert templates for CS. Build a short playbook and a template PagerDuty alert to recommend automatic rollback thresholds (e.g., >2x median latency sustained for 5 minutes). Deliverable: playbook doc + 1 sample PD rule. Owner: Aisha Patel (CS).

Customer-impact estimations (heuristic):
- Fixing cold-start tail could reduce P99 spikes by ~35% for 10–12 customers currently reporting user-visible regressions (estimated uplift to NPS for those accounts).
- Better KV-cache doc + SDK snippets could lower accidental token spend for 5 large customers by ~8–12% when they adopt explicit invalidation patterns.

Open questions + things to validate:
- To what extent are Dedicated and Hosted showing the same kernel-selection overhead? Need logs (trace-level) from both environments. (Ticket: JIRA-OPS-8792).
- Are spikes correlated with autoscaler activity or with model-variant evictions? (Trace + infra metrics needed).
- Should we expose manual cache-invalidation APIs or keep the API surface minimal and instead recommend TTL-based best-practices?

Patch ideas (low-risk, implementable quickly):
- Add a Console banner that shows the currently selected fallback model for each route and the last model-change time. Quick dev: console change + small API call to fetch route config. Benefits: reduces confusion when canaries swap.
- Add a flag in SDKs: force_cache_bypass=true (default false) to let devs experiment quickly. Ship as beta in py/js SDKs with a clear warning.
- Small runtime tweak: measure and log (not alert) kernel-selection time as a separate metric per request so we can correlate with customer reports without changing behavior.

Risks and cautions:
- Any kernel-loading optimization needs careful validation across quantized variants — wrong assumptions can break numeric parity. Route-level exposure of fallbacks needs security review (do we leak internal variant names?).
- Cache invalidation surface expands attack/abuse vectors (a malicious client could flood invalidations). If we expose APIs, require tenant-auth and rate-limiting.

Suggested next steps (immediate, owners assigned):
- Today (CS): create customer follow-up pack for top 6 flagged accounts (Aisha). Include short survey asking for request sizes, typical idle times, and whether they use Dedicated or Hosted. Due: Jun 23.
- This week (Eng): start Dedicated profiler spike (Evan) — gather traces by Jun 19.
- Next week (Product/Console): mock three policy presets and build telemetry preview concept (Miguel) — initial mock due Jun 25.
- Docs (CS): draft KV-cache KB and SDK snippet (Priya) — publish draft Jun 20.

Notes to self / shorthand tasks (scratch):
- Pull traces from Jun 1–Jun 8 tagged with "coldstart" or kernel-load. (JIRA-OPS-8792).
- Cross-reference customer billing anomalies before/after canary swaps (ops-fin).
- Slack: post summary + request for help in #eng-serving-runtime w/ trace sample.

Appendix: sample customer quotes (verbatim):
- "It's hard to trust the Hosted route when we saw the canary silently use a slower model — we lost a demo" — CSM notes, Jun 8.
- "We need a way to say: 'always prefer the cheaper model for background jobs'" — engineering lead, marketplace SaaS, May 29.
- "When we roll out a new model, keys in cache seem to change; our app duplicated tokens for 3 minutes" — infra engineer, healthcare, Jun 6.

End-of-notes.
If you want I can convert this into a 1-pager for execs (Aisha) or expand the probe plan into JIRA tasks (Evan + Miguel).
